name: Syria

facts.religion: Sunni Islam about 74%, Alawite, Christian, Druze and Ismaili minorities

system_note: A transitional system giving the interim president broad powers for five years.
snapshot: Ahmed al-Sharaa's new government won sanctions relief from Washington but fought the Kurdish-led SDF in January before a deal on merging them into the state.
culture: Damascus and Aleppo are among the oldest continuously inhabited cities, and Syria's souks, mosques and Roman ruins at Palmyra testify to millennia of history. Syrian cuisine, from kibbeh to Aleppo pepper dishes, and its TV dramas were loved across the Arab world. Its mix of Sunni, Alawite, Christian, Druze and Kurdish communities makes sectarian relations central.
society: The 2011 to 2024 civil war killed about half a million people and displaced half the population, and millions of refugees are weighing whether to return. Sanctions relief has opened the door to reconstruction. Massacres of Alawites on the coast in 2025 and fighting with Druze in Sweida exposed sectarian dangers in the new order.
situation: In December 2024, rebels led by Ahmed al-Sharaa, a former al-Qaeda commander, toppled Bashar al-Assad, ending 54 years of his family's rule and a civil war that killed half a million people. Al-Sharaa has since swapped fatigues for suits and won over Trump, who met him in the White House and promised to lift sanctions. In December 2025 Congress repealed the Caesar Act sanctions, conditional on protecting minorities and fighting ISIS. In 2026 the test of those conditions was the Kurds.

The Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces, America's main ground ally against ISIS, have run the northeast for a decade and agreed in March 2025 to merge into the new state, but little happened. In January, government forces and Turkish-backed factions attacked SDF areas near Aleppo and seized Tabqa; dozens of Kurds were killed, and video showed fighters toppling a statue of a female Kurdish fighter (Fox News). Senator Lindsey Graham threatened to revive the sanctions "even more bone crushing" (Rudaw). A ceasefire on 18 January held unevenly. Then the integration process moved: in February, Syria's foreign minister and SDF commander Mazloum Abdi met Secretary of State Rubio together in Munich, and Damascus and the SDF began joint management of Qamishli airport and the Rmeilan oil fields (Enab Baladi). Syria has joined the anti-ISIS coalition, and the sectarian killings of Alawites and Druze in 2025 still shadow its new government.
power: A transitional presidential system under a 2025 constitutional declaration giving al-Sharaa broad powers for five years. A People's Assembly was chosen in 2025 through indirect selection, with a third appointed by the president.
holders: Interim President Ahmed al-Sharaa, since January 2025.
